gaps.sentence: He stayed ___ touch with every colleague he'd ever had.
She's ___ charge of the whole marketing department.
The play closed after three nights ___ account of poor ticket sales.
gaps.explanation: 'On account of' = because of, in a formal register.

gaps.sentence: ___ first, the plan sounded ridiculous — then it grew on us.
gaps.explanation: 'At first' = in the beginning (contrast with 'first' = before anything else).

gaps.sentence: Everything happened ___ such short notice that we panicked.
___ reference to your letter of 12 May, we are still processing the claim.
gaps.explanation: 'With reference to' introduces the subject of a formal letter.

gaps.sentence: He acted on his own ___ and did not ask permission.
gaps.hint: on your own ___ = without being told
gaps.explanation: 'On one's own initiative' = deciding and acting independently.

gaps.sentence: There's no point arguing ___ it now — the contract is signed.
